notes.title: Regional Price Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Today, we're approving and locking in Steam's latest regional price recommendations on our games. Some of these new prices are a big change (check out the full list [url=https://steamdb.info/blog/valve-price-matrix-2022-update/#29-99-usd]here[/url]), so I want to give a little context.

For those who are unaware, Steam doesn't simply use exchange rates to set prices. In a nutshell, they try and consider many factors so that, hopefully, the average consumer pays a fairer price in each country. Read more about their policy [url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/pricing#5]here[/url]. 

We trust Steam with this; we always have, locking in Steam's recommended prices on all our games since we started publishing on the store back in 2015 - the alternative being to set, manage, and update prices manually across 30+ countries ourselves. As we understand it, Steam's new changes should account for all the crazy fluctuations in the worldwide economy over the past few years.

Special mention to fans in countries where the price changes are more dramatic - Turkey and Argentina, especially: we see you and appreciate you, and apologize if these changes affect you negatively. 

What I can say is that we saw a huge increase in sales in your countries last year, but no increase in the number of players. Something like 85% of sales coming "from Argentina and Turkey" seem to be coming from people playing in other countries - people who are chasing the lowest possible price on Steam. This is apparently a widespread problem on Steam, which is why Steam is recommending an especially large increase in your regional prices. 

This is not an easy decision, but we do agree with it - the alternative is basically encouraging people to abuse the system and pay far less for our games than we know they're worth. Thanks very much for understanding.

- Rodrigue and the Thunder Lotus Team

p.s. Unrelated but very important side note for y'all: please spare a kind thought for the people of Syria and Turkey, who experienced a devastating earthquake this week! We've made a donation to [url=https://donate.redcross.ca/page/121799/donate/1?locale=en-CA]The Red Cross[/url] to support relief efforts in the region; if you're able, please consider doing the same. To our friends in the region, we hope you're safe and sound. ːstella_heartsː

notes.title: Have a wonderful Holiday Season! - Recap of the Year 2022
notes.content:
[h1]Happy Holidays![/h1]

Hey everyone!

Another year has flown on by, it's time for us to look back and reminisce on just about everything that happened in [b]2022[/b]... but [i]first[/i], I'd like to thank each and every one of you who have been supporting us, be it through reading my shenanigans, playing our games, making art, or being involved in our community. Your passion for games gives us the fuel to keep on burning as bright as ever! We really wouldn't be here without you! 🥰

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/b7dd0444460f576330d60991948789e07019a980.png[/img]

Now, without further ado, let's dig into our recap of [b]2022[/b]!

[h1]Start of 2022 - Winter[/h1]

The year started off [i]fairly[/i] smoothly.
With the busy release of the [b]Spiritfarer's Farewell Edition[/b] at the end of [b]2021[/b], we figured we'd take some time to recuperate and properly prepare the rest of the year.

[h2]Spiritfarer Poll[/h2]

With the release of the [url=https://www.fangamer.com/products/spiritfarer-plush-daffodil]Daffodil plushie[/url] last year, I figured it'd be [b][i]fun[/i][/b] to see which other spirit you'd like to see as a plushie. Figured it'd be fun to showcase my findings.

Since I figured ranking 10+ characters in order of most to least [i]huggable[/i] would be a nightmare to decypher (and answer 😰), I narrowed it down to [b]Alice, Atul, Stanley and Summer[/b], and sent it to our [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/newsletter/]Mailing List[/url]. With ~ 7000 votes compiled, the battle raged on and, in a rather convincing fashion, [b]Atul[/b] was crowned our winner! 🐸

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/8319d48acaaf52ca6ca04b49877e73088d25d8d2.png[/img]

[h2]Surveys[/h2]

Through this experience with the [b]poll[/b], I've came to realize that I did not know [i]much[/i] about [b]who[/b] was reading my emails & blogposts, so I've started cooking up some fun small~ish surveys for our [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/newsletter/]Mailing List[/url] audience to answer, in order to could learn a bit more about who they are, where they're from, what they enjoy playing, etc.

While there were no big surprises to share, it did confirm my suspicions that I was indeed talking to an amazing group of lovely gamers 🥰

Big thanks to everyone that answered my silly surveys!

[url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/newsletter/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/3e0f07751a619f9418b98b35769d9083c3804771.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Spring[/h1]

[h2]New Office[/h2]

We officially moved into a new, bigger office in the Saint-Henri neighborhood of [b]Montréal, Québec[/b].

It's a really lovely place, with a lot of open space, a gym and an outdoor pool!
We still haven't [i]fully[/i] made this place our own [i]just yet[/i], so I won't share any pictures, but we love it very much and we can't wait to share how it will look once we're done!

With it, we changed our routine from full remote, to two in-office days, which took a bit of getting used to, but we're all pretty happy with our current arrangements 😊👍🏻

I get to see trains go by every hour. 🚂

[h2]Discord Events[/h2]

Soon after, [b]Discord[/b] released a new feature called [b]Events[/b] to all servers, so it seemed fun to try it out with [url=discord.gg/tlg]our community[/url].

Given my lack of culture of [i]Ghibli movies[/i], which were a huge inspiration for [b]Spiritfarer[/b], I figured I'd remediate the situation and host some movie watchalongs in our [url=discord.gg/tlg]Public Discord[/url]. We'd get ourselves our own version of the film, synchronize on my timer and react together. We watched movies like [b]Spirited Away[/b] and [b]Kiki's Delivery Service[/b].

It was a lot of fun, thanks to everyone that joined and hung out!
We also created an [b]Events[/b] channel, for those interested in hosting their own event for the [url=discord.gg/tlg]Discord community[/url]!

[url=discord.gg/tlg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/8ec6b13ec57b2289332003053ce39788eb0524d7.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Fall[/h1]

[h2]Soundtrack Update & Blogpost[/h2]

The long awaited, and often requested, [b]Soundtrack Update[/b] was pushed live in mid-November, adding a lot of the missing tracks that were added with the [b]Lily, Beverly, Jackie & Daria[/b] updates.

To commemorate this moment, and the shipment of the soundtrack's [b]Vinyls[/b], I sat down with [url=https://maxll.ca/]MaxLL[/url], our amazingly talented friend and composer, to talk about his processes while making the Soundtrack, and posted his answers in a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/972660/view/3407563661873389396]Blogpost[/url].

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/972660/view/3407563661873389396][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/e0bb13bf1d589f05a85c353fd9d57a75d0da2127.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Artbook[/h2]

Alongside the [b]Soundtrack[/b], we figured we'd take a stab at updating the game's [b]Artbook[/b], to add the post-release content contained in the [b]Farewell Edition[/b].

Curious to know more about the [b]Spiritfarer[/b] universe, see amazing high resolution art of all the locals & characters, and read about our inspirations? The [b]updated Artbook[/b] is available [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1398770/Spiritfarer_Farewell_Edition__Digital_Artbook/]here on Steam[/url]!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1398770/Spiritfarer_Farewell_Edition__Digital_Artbook/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/fc68c676881bb4cd79278da0d1e8c0349b67787a.png[/img][/url]

[h1]End of 2022[/h1]

[h2]Discord documentary[/h2]

In early November, [b]Discord[/b] approached us with a fun proposition to highlight our [url=discord.gg/tlg]Discord community[/url] in a mini-documentary, focusing on [b]Spiritfarer[/b]. We wholeheartedly accepted!

For the video, some members of the [b]Spiritfarer[/b] team, two of moderators, a handful of community members and I had the wonderful pleasure of discussing with a lovely member of [b]Discord[/b]'s staff, about how our server came to be, how it has evolved in the last few years and how it has impacted our lives.

The video was released in early December and was teased at the [b]Game Awards 2022[/b].
If you haven't already, we highly recommend you to watch the video and join our [url=discord.gg/tlg]amazing community[/url]. 💖

[previewyoutube=8Yh5AwmjEwY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Games We Loved 2022[/h2]

As always, we posted a list of all our [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/2022-the-games-we-loved/]favorite games[/url] we played this year! If you're looking for things to do during your holidays, I highly recommend you to check it out!

[url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/2022-the-games-we-loved/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/629c042ff58746d3dfd61c2e212d33735d56203d.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Plans for 2023?[/h1]

We're now days away from the start of [b]2023[/b].

[i]Truthfully[/i], there will be a lot going on next year, a lot of things I'm [b][u]super excited[/u][/b] about, but a lot of things I'll be unable to share with you [i]until the time is right[/i]. We'll be taking two weeks~ish off to rest and prepare ourselves for the exciting new adventures that awaits us. We hope to see you there! 🥳

If you want to stay up to date with our news, I highly recommend you sign up for our [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/newsletter/]mailing list[/url], if you haven't already!

[h1]Thanks for reading![/h1]

Okay, that's all I have for [b]2022[/b].

Thanks again for all the support, it really means a lot to us! Your passion for videogames grants us the ability to continue making what we love! Thank you for playing!

Stay happy, stay healthy and please don't forget to take care of yourself! Have a happy holiday season & a happy New Year!
See you in 2023!

Many hugs,

notes.title: Making Spiritfarer's Soundtrack | Max LL
notes.content:
[h3]Hey Spiritfarers![/h3]

To celebrate the long awaited [b]Soundtrack update[/b], which contains the theme for all the new [b]spirits[/b], [b]islands[/b] and [b]event[/b] (and some missing songs from the original game), I sat down with [url=https://maxll.ca/]Max LL[/url], our wonderful composer, to ask him some questions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/7c00b3e74d79028fe49d08aaa762e7c6d829794f.png[/img]
[i]Max LL[/i] - [url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BvyxmurgLd7/]Instagram[/url]

[h2]What is your history with Thunder Lotus?[/h2]

Will (the studio’s founder) and I are childhood friends. We used to play in a rock/metal band together in high school, Will as drummer and I as guitarist and singer. We share some great memories from that time. Those were also very formative years for me as a musician, I started trying my hand at writing, composition and experimented with different musical styles.

A few years later, as Will was contemplating the idea of starting a game studio, I was making my first steps in the film and game industry as a composer. We had kept playing music together through the years and it felt natural for us to collaborate on a first project, so Will asked me if I was interested in writing a musical theme for [b]Jotun[/b], which was still in its early conception phase. A [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/thunderlotusgames/jotun]Kickstarter campaign[/url] was launched, successfully funded, and this is what started this beautiful collaborative working relationship I’ve had with the Thunder Lotus team since.

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c1_tiDJJpA4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/78273db231e4bcfdad3ea7090f51b8a25064ecc9.png[/img][/url]
[i]Max LL, Ulric Corbeil Trudel & Ian Lafontaine working on Jotun's sound design.[/i]

[h2]How would you define the music you created for Spiritfarer?[/h2]

I’m not the most eloquent communicator when it comes to describing music with words. Music can evoke an infinitely nuanced, complex and colorful array of emotional worlds in a way that other mediums cannot.

For [b]Spiritfarer[/b], it was important for the music to have both complexity and simplicity at the same time and an intrinsic emotional duality, even sometimes dichotomy. Grief is a complex and difficult subject matter that the studio wanted to portray in a cozy and lighthearted way. Thunder Lotus wanted the game to help us free ourselves from some of the taboos surrounding death and passing. The music needed to reflect that, so it could never be just happy, angry, or sad. Sometimes, moments of happiness needed to be accompanied by a form of melancholy, moments of fear and sadness by nostalgia. Finding the right tone for some of the game’s moments was definitely a challenge but I think I eventually landed in an emotional space that felt right. I tried deeply reconnecting with all the moments of grief I had gone through in my life to summon the appropriate musical energy.

In general, I’d say that the kind of music I had to write for [b]Spiritfarer[/b] is one that comes most naturally to me and that made the project such a joy to work on. 

[url=https://maxll.ca/sheetmusic][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/e48127ded9899ef96e62216e21652eda30d06993.png[/img][/url]
[i]Spiritfarer's Sheet music[/i] - [url=https://maxll.ca/sheetmusic]Max LL[/url]

[h2]What were your inspirations for the soundtrack, and how did you choose which instrument(s) to use?[/h2]

[b]Nicolas Guérin[/b], Spiritfarer’s creative director, shared a wide selection of songs with me at the beginning of the project. The genres ranged from manouche guitar, jazz and french folk to [i]Ghibli film scores[/i] and 20th century classical piano music. We decided early on that piano was going to be heavily featured in the soundtrack. Indeed, piano is an instrument that feels very familiar and “cozy” in the western world as it is common for families to have one in their home. Stella plays acoustic/nylon guitar in the game, so that also became an obvious instrument of choice. Luckily for me, those are the two instruments I’m most comfortable with. Although coincidently, those instruments had not been used in any of the studio’s previous games. Playing guitar and piano for Spiritfarer felt like coming back home after a long trip abroad.

A wide variety of other instruments was also featured in the score: [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitar]sitar[/url], mandolin, [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammered_dulcimer]dulcimer[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakuhachi]shakuhachi[/url], singing bowls, to name a few. The traditional orchestral sound was used to blend those textures and colours with the guitar and piano. It’s always present in a way that adds a more complex and profound emotional underscore when needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/348b635dad193d5aeceb95349fc60f7f1d6975c4.png[/img]
[i]Max LL's creative space[/i] - [url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CGIXMw7H_mh/]Instagram[/url]

Some of the tracks were also written as duets. Conversations are an important part of the storytelling process, so it felt natural to have instruments “speaking” to each other, asking questions and answering, conversating (for ex.: the tracks [i]Gurenu Fields[/i], [i]At Night[/i] and [i]Hummingberg[/i]).

[h2]Can you walk me through the process of creating a track?[/h2]

The creative process was different for each track, but it always came back to connecting emotionally with the subject matter of the moment. I try speaking a language with music that most people, even if they don't understand it fully, will be able to feel. Everyone will experience the game and music differently based on their own life experiences and upbringing. A big part of my work was bringing to life the emotions that the characters inside the game were experiencing. If the player can relate to those characters, he will most likely experience those emotions as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/165be60096ae1b146e3207728119ec5c584456fd.jpg[/img]
[i]What Will You Leave Behind[/i] - [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZfqGU6Y5uU]Spiritfarer's Animated trailer[/url]

For [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-GHvj04iyU]What Will You Leave Behind[/url], I originally wrote the first version of the song for the [b]animated trailer[/b] that was launched a few months before the release of the game. The team had contemplated the idea of covering a well-known song, but I felt it was worth trying doing something original before venturing into licensing territory. I took a couple of days to write some lyrics and a first draft of the song. However, words on a page, an instrumental demo and asking the team to use their imagination wasn’t going to cut it. I needed to communicate the idea as clearly and convincingly as possible. This was at the beginning of the pandemic, we were all in lockdown and I didn’t have access to my usual network of musicians. So I asked my partner Maude, who has a beautiful calming voice, to sing the song in an acoustic demo I produced.

The team fell in love with the song and were convinced an original track was the way to go. The animation style of the trailer called for a dynamic orchestral score and therefore, for a voice that was going to be able to soar over the ensemble. I emailed Timbre, a talented soprano singer and harpist who’s music I truly adore, to ask if she was interested to work remotely on the project. She agreed, we were absolutely thrilled by her performance and the trailer was received with great enthusiasm in the community.

Will mentioned to me a few times how much he would’ve loved hearing a calmer version of the song that had the same kind of intimacy the original demo he had fallen in love with had. I told him I’d try my hand at rearranging the song for the end credits if time allowed at the end of the project. So two weeks before the release of the game, I rewrote [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lnzL_O82nvc]What Will You Leave Behind[/url] for piano and strings and asked Maude if she could once again lend us her beautiful voice for the performance. This became the song you hear when you finish the game and it’s truly heartwarming to witness how much it has touched and moved people everywhere around the world. In retrospect, it’s also one of the pieces of music I’m most proud of. Whenever I hear it, it brings back so many emotions from that particular moment of my life. 

[h2]What were your intentions behind Alex the Seal’s [i]infamous[/i] theme?[/h2]

When I asked Nico to describe to me who [b]Alex the Seal[/b] was, he told me he was a kind of annoying bus driver. I wanted to try something a little different, so I took a more radical approach and went a little crazy!

The irritating honking imposed itself and the percussion ensemble was a way to evoke the circus-like nature of his behavior. The out-of-tune trumpet felt like the proper instrument to act as his “voice” and I added some cheesy vocals because [b]Alex[/b] felt like the kind of person who’d constantly be singing in a [i]dooo dooo[/i] rhythmic manner while “driving” without too much regard for pitch. The resulting music is quite annoying, but that was all part of the original concept and it was a lot of fun to write! 

[url=https://youtu.be/JZTKFiCMA-o?t=2766][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/6b94dd2782755521deca9752dd81433e7d803c70.png[/img][/url]
[i]Alex the Seal[/i]

[h2]What are your thoughts on the game / soundtrack's success?[/h2]

The game was released a few months into the pandemic, one could say that it came at the right time and became a blessing for a lot of people who were trying to deal with a difficult moment in their lives. However, when the game launched, we were all apart, remote, separated. It made the moment very uneventful. We could see in the numbers that people were interested in the game but it all felt very impersonal and abstract.

Nonetheless, since then, the team and I have been submerged by an unbelievable amount of truly moving comments and messages from fans about how the game and music had helped them in a difficult moment in their lives. Some of the unbelievable testimonials we’ve received have been both heartbreaking and heartwarming. I’m so humbled and grateful when people take the time to write about their stories. I would love to be out there to personally support everyone that’s been through hardship, but I have to accept that it’s impossible. It’s comforting to know that the game and its music are now out into the world doing a little bit of good.

[b]Spiritfarer[/b] is not only the studio’s project now, it has left home, has a life of its own and now belongs to everyone who wants to experience it. The initial launch was slightly bittersweet because of the circumstances I described above, but I think we all now all realize that Spiritfarer is a special project that we were all lucky to be a part of. 

[url=https://www.iam8bit.com/collections/vinyl/products/spiritfarer-vinyl-soundtrack][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/53137d99c5d459ec980f2b30afcf986c0be660d8.png[/img][/url]
[i]Spiritfarer's vinyl[/i] - [url=https://www.iam8bit.com/collections/vinyl/products/spiritfarer-vinyl-soundtrack]iam8bit[/url]

[h2]Any final thoughts you'd like to share with your fans?[/h2]

To everyone out there who has been moved by Spiritfarer, who took the time to play the game, to listen to the music, to write to us, or share their stories, I would simply like to thank you from the bottom of my heart. And no matter the challenges you are going through, there are always ways to find support, don’t give up, the hard times will pass. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/b5946462319184613e371f3ba8fc43829ee2e23f.png[/img]

[h3]Thank you so much for the Music, Max LL[/h3]
We truly appreciate the wonderful work you've contributed to our games over the years and are looking forward to our next projects together!

-Med and the Thunder Lotus team

notes.title: Xbox Game Pass is losing some brilliant games soon
notes.content:
The latest titles to come to Xbox Game Pass have been announced, and while there's some good titles on the way, it's also that time of the month again where we commiserate the great games that are soon to be leaving.

Amongst the titles leaving is NBA 2K22, Two Point Hospital, and Elite: Dangerous. So, I've bad news for both avid space explorers, basketball pros, and hospital managers alike, as all three will be bidding farewell to Xbox Games Pass on August 31.

This isn't all, either. There's truly a cracking line-up of titles leaving in just a couple of weeks, which consists of a few quaint but enjoyable indie titles. These include Spiritfarer, Twelve Minutes, What Remains of Edith Finch, and Signs of the Sojourner.

notes.title: Happy Holidays - Recap of the year 2021
notes.content:
[h1]Happy Holidays, from the Thunder Lotus family![/h1]

Hey everyone!

Another year comes to a close, time to take you on a journey down memory lane to reminisce on everything that happened in [b]2021[/b]... but [i]first[/i], I'd like to extend our deepest and most sincere gratitude to each and every one of you, we really wouldn't be where we are now if not for all of your love and support.

Please stay the [b]best darn community[/b] we've ever seen! ːstella_heartsː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/fd696fab34831fe3c15da2af50160ce6da751793.png[/img]

[h1]Start of 2021 - Winter[/h1]

At the start of the year, we unveiled the plans that we set in motion in [i]November of 2020[/i].

We had reached out to our lovely [url=discord.gg/tlg]Discord community[/url] for their feedback on what they'd like for us to make in [b]2021[/b] for [b]Spiritfarer[/b] and, after a few months of discussion, upvotes and deliberating, we finally locked in our plans for the year, based on our interests and their feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/2fce4d0dd007ec5521fc623955f24c69e6e2bfbf.png[/img]

At the start of [b]February[/b], once everything was ready, we thanked them by sending them a quick sneak peak of what would become our future roadmap.

A week later, our official [b]2021 Roadmap[/b] was released!

We announced [i]three[/i] major free content updates for [b]Spiritfarer[/b], each releasing during a different season this year.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/972660/view/3040462341844559100][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/ca661b36de16074feff51a102ab3f04600a1678c.png[/img][/url]

Now, all that was left to do was to actually make them!

[h1]Spring[/h1]

[b]Spring[/b] was the real start of what would be a very busy year. In [b]April[/b], we released our first content update: the [b]Lily Update[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/7390db7ea294569cc02752dec74d9089ba90b707.png[/img]

Although it was the [i]smallest[/i], this update brought a major change to the way we handled the ending of the game, by giving a lot more context to our lovely protagonist's life prior to the start of the game.

We were pretty ecstatic and wanted to share this important milestone with everyone! With the pandemic and the weather being what it was, we couldn't realistically do it in person... but we were in luck! An online convention was just on the horizon: [b]LudoNarraCon[/b]

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fUZ0oA9WX2A&list=PLvvApHEe2-gu5NF8ctAuAfIVhYA1QEnbL][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/5fefa0d97df229d19d348b34b119cad9efac1fbd.png[/img][/url]

I was joined by [b]Jo[/b], our Art Director, and [b]Nicolas[/b], our Creative Director, in our [i]first[/i] real online convention! I hosted an hour-long talk show [i]each day[/i] of the convention, where we answered questions about Spiritfarer, its world and its creation. If you haven't already, you can watch all of it on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fUZ0oA9WX2A&list=PLvvApHEe2-gu5NF8ctAuAfIVhYA1QEnbL]YouTube[/url], but be warned that there's lots of spoilers!

[h1]Summer[/h1]

Our [b]Summer[/b] was buuuusy.

It started out with a bang with [b]Summer Games Done Quick[/b]! [url=https://www.twitch.tv/jevilevee]JeviLevee[/url] invited me to sit on his virtual couch during the show, where he showcased how he achieved the any% world record [url=https://www.speedrun.com/sundered]speedrun[/url] of [b]Sundered[/b], directly from the [i]online[/i] big stage! His luck was [i]unreal[/i] and the run was amazing!

Thanks again for the invite! The [url=https://discord.gg/vHRDAkX]Sundered speedrunning community[/url] is proud of you! 🥳

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hhv7u7II8jg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/18bd0d31b237fccc01d356c6d586eb421fef48ba.jpg[/img][/url]

Then, [url=https://twitter.com/MaxLLMusic/status/1416061817709867009]Max LL[/url], our awesome friend and the composer for our games, released a brand [url=https://maxll.ca/sheetmusic]new sheet music[/url] for What Will You Leave Behind (end credit song for Spiritfarer)!

[url=https://maxll.ca/sheetmusic][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/71c625844a3b9d07727ff6d706567efc67ad0197.jpg[/img][/url]

Shortly after, [b]TheEscapist[/b] premiered their [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qxx8sEGjntI]Documentary on Spiritfarer[/url], where the team and I reminisced about how Spiritfarer came to be and its release's impact on us moving forward. Being a big fan of Yahtzee, it was such a surreal journey for all of us to say the least!

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qxx8sEGjntI][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/dacfee444d7128ac54130e540d14a3edf432dbce.png[/img][/url]

[b]Summer[/b] ended with the planned release of the [b]Beverly Update[/b]. It brought our first full-length spirit story to Spiritfarer and a slew of much needed quality of life changes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/348e1bc87aa94ecd5e32511bc622c0d553fe3a55.png[/img]

[h1]Fall[/h1]

[i]Spooky season[/i] started with a heavier note this year.

We kept true to our promise and, in late [b]September[/b], we finally released the revised version of [b]Gustav[/b]'s story, with the help and feedback from our wonderful panel of disabled individuals. We'd like to take the time to thanks them again for sharing their viewpoints and enriching our own, and shoutout to [url=https://ablegamers.org/]AbleGamers[/url] for putting us in contact with these lovely people.

[url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/gustav/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/6530e6bbd46ad52af2f222da3e6a941d270f8c23.png[/img][/url]

Then, we had the pleasure of announcing our partnership with [url=https://www.fangamer.com/collections/spiritfarer]FanGamer[/url] in the creation of a [url=https://www.fangamer.com/collections/spiritfarer/products/spiritfarer-shirt-stella]Spiritfarer Shirt[/url] (out now!) and a [url=https://www.fangamer.com/collections/spiritfarer/products/spiritfarer-plush-daffodil]Daffodil Plushie[/url] (coming next year 👀)!

[url=https://www.fangamer.com/collections/spiritfarer][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/bbffdb7a36f01412fb27fd2990324435682256be.jpg[/img][/url]

And finally, we announced the release date for our last update, the [b]Jackie & Daria Update[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/b427efc353c79bdd7dd23c756d786c677e19fb65.png[/img]

Since this was by far the largest update we had planned for the game, we wanted to make it [i]special![/i]

It contained two additional full-length storyline for these two spirits, on a brand new island with a new event to experience! As grand as it was, being the last update, we wanted to make it [i]extra[/i] with a proper send-off.

[h1]Farewell Edition[/h1]

[b]December[/b] finally arrived and the time to say farewell was upon us... to the year [b]2021[/b], but also to something more than just a project.

By this point, we had decided that we'd be parting ways with [b]Spiritfarer[/b] after this [b]last[/b] update and, now that it was ready to be released, we decided it needed to be sent off with a big celebration. That's when the [b]Farewell Edition[/b] came to be. Let's take some time to reflect on all that happened.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/d7546bea8e82f27fbdd083606a3314b9e4ba9596.png[/img]

From its inception in 2018, its announcement at E3 in 2019, its release amidst a global pandemic in 2020, its three content updates this year... to its eventual conclusion, [b]Spiritfarer[/b] was an epic journey we will not soon forget. Truthfully, making this game really helped us work through a lot of memories (good & bad) and remind us of loved ones we lost. It helped us experience feelings we had yet to fully embrace and create new memories. It helped us bond with others whose experiences matched our own. And it helped us grow!

Side note, being [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/972660/Spiritfarer_Farewell_Edition/]Overwhelmingly Positive[/url] is nothing short of amazing! ːstella_heartsː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/d0db3fa7d32fb9a3821929abd3fb271c5c55a842.gif[/img]

Thank you for taking this adventure with us, genuinely. Whether you played through [b]Spiritfarer[/b], watched a playthrough, recommended to friends, or reached out to share your experiences with us directly, thank you. Without your support, we wouldn't be where we are today! You made all this possible and made this journey all the more worthwhile!

[b]Thank you![/b]

[h1]End of 2021[/h1]

Now that the year is finally over, our yearly tradition is back! As you might know, we like to share the love for this wonderful industry by listing the favorite games we played [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/2017-the-games-we-loved/]each year[/url]! This year is no exception! Go check out the [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/2021-the-games-we-loved/]games we enjoyed in 2021[/url]!

We're now a lot of people, so there's something for every taste! You might even find something fun to try during this holiday period!

[url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/2021-the-games-we-loved/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/cbd43ddaafbbe722bd68cbcc0b9df0db7ab8cf7b.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Plans for 2022?[/h1]

First off, we'll be moving into a [b]brand new office[/b] in [b]January[/b]!

Although the pandemic hasn't fully let up (and we're still mostly working from home), our company has grown so much over the last two years that we no longer fit in our old building! We're so excited to enter the new building, it even has an [i]outdoor swimming pool?[/i] 🤿

[i]Game Development[/i] wise, the [b]Spiritfarer[/b] Team is now going to be working full time on a [b]brand new exciting project[/b]! Unfortunately, there's still a lot of work before we're ready to unveil anything, but we can barely contain our excitement for you to see what we've been working on! You'll have to stay tuned!

If you want to stay up to date with our news, I highly recommend you sign up for our [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/newsletter]mailing list[/url], or follow [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/thunderlotus]our Developer Page[/url] if you haven't already!

[h1]Thanks for reading![/h1]

Now here we are... days before the year 2022.

What a year it's been. It started with only [i]three key events[/i] in mind, and it feels like [b]so much[/b] happened! Again, thank you so much for the support! Thanks for permitting us to share out passion for videogames with the world, and [b]thank you for playing[/b]!

Stay happy stay healthy, have a happy holiday season and a happy New Year!
See you in 2022!

Lots of love,
-Med and the Thunder Lotus team

notes.title: Hades wins first Hugo Award in new video game category
notes.content:
The Hugo Awards announced the first winner of its newly created Best Video Game award, and it’s Hades, the roguelite action RPG from developer Supergiant Games. Though the Hugo Awards is a literary awards show dedicated to science fiction and fantasy, this year it branched out into the world of video games and gave Hades another chance to make history.

Supergiant creative director Greg Kasavin reacted to his studio’s game winning a Hugo Award in a tweet, expressing regret that he couldn’t be there to accept on behalf of the team, but shared his gratitude at video games finally having a space at the storied awards show and thanking it for his studio’s work in particular.

Other games nominated for the historic first prize were Final Fantasy 7 Remake, The Last of Us: Part 2, Spiritfarer, Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and Blaseball, all 2020 games, as the Hugo Awards looks at works from the previous year.

notes.content:
Thunder Lotus announced that their gorgeous 2D management simulator Spiritfarer sold a million copies, making the indie game an undeniable success. They also marked the occasion to coincide with the launch of the Farewell Edition, closing the book on Spiritfarer for good.

The game whose developer describes it as a “cozy management game about dying” released to rave reviews in 2020 and featured regular free content updates that added more spirits to ferry to the afterlife and expanded the already expansive world of the game. Farewell Edition brings together all the content updates with the base game for a complete experience.

The latest content update is also now available. The Jackie and Daria Update adds a new island, two new spirits, and a new event. This will be the last content update the game will receive, hence why the definitive edition release is dubbed the Farewell Edition.

notes.title: Cozy afterlife sim Spiritfarer bids goodbye with a final update
notes.content:
Spiritfarer, a cozy (after)life sim about ferrying the recently departed to their eternal rest, is ready to move on after selling more than a million copies since its launch last year. The charming management game received its final update today, along with a new complete edition.

Spiritfarer: Farewell Edition is a free update for Spiritfarer, and includes all the previously released updates to Thunder Lotus' charming game. The latest, the Jackie & Daria update, is the largest of the bunch - it adds a "fun, albeit vulgar" hyena named Jackie and Daria, the erratic bat.

The update also includes a new island, Overbrook, where Jackie formerly worked as a hospital caretaker. There's a new event called Mind Palace, new recipes to craft, and a beehive you can add to your station. Of course, there's plenty to get up to on Overbrook island as well, and both Jackie and Daria are sure to have their own sweetly heart wrenching stories to dig into. You'll be able to head that way after uncovering the mist near Oxbury and receiving a letter from Jackie, asking for your help.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: В загробный мир с лёгким сердцем: Обзор Spiritfarer
notes.content: В нынешние времена разработчики высокобюджетных проектов зачастую опасаются рисковать и экспериментировать с жанрами, стараясь держаться ближе к проверенным трендам и наиболее выгодным с коммерческой точки зрения решениям. В таких условиях почти все самобытные игры, выходящие за рамки общепринятых тенденций, создаются независимыми студиями, и часто, к сожалению, просто игнорируются потенциальной аудиторией. Spiritfarer от канадцев из Thunder Lotus Games (компания является как разработчиком, так и издателем) как раз относится к тем редким случаям, когда игру нельзя подогнать к определённой категории или направлению.

notes.title: Lily Update is out now!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/b5946462319184613e371f3ba8fc43829ee2e23f.png[/img]

[h1]Lily Update is Live![/h1]

Hey there, Spiritfarers!

The [b]Lily Update[/b] is ready to [i]spread its wings[/i], and [b]Lily[/b] is finally making her debut to the [b]Spiritfarer[/b] crew! This update is completely [u][b][i]free[/i][/b][/u]! All you need to do is [b]Update Spiritfarer[/b]! ːstella_happyː

Alongside [b]Lily[/b] herself, you'll find some [b]new features[/b], a bunch of [b]Quality of life changes[/b] and lots of [b]Bug Fixes[/b]! You'll want to stick to the end, I have a handful of [b]news[/b] that you won't want to miss!

Oh and, before I forget, here's the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9TGG72zmsA][b]Lily Update trailer[/b][/url]:
[previewyoutube=j9TGG72zmsA;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Content Update[/h2]

Before we dig into the [i]meat and potatoes[/i] of this update, I wanted to let you know that we decided to make the [b]Lily Update[/b] a bit smaller than the others in order to properly take the time and address the most common feedback we received since the game's release: [b]Stella[/b]'s Story and [b]Spiritfarer's Ending[/b].

We heard it loud and clear, and we agreed, so we really gave it our all to make [b]Stella[/b]'s story and its conclusion more satisfying. We're really happy with how it turned out, and we hope you'll enjoy it too!

Now, without further ado, here's [b]Lily[/b], the Butterfly Spirit!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/574e7552841a96d2c1fec356f128e79b28349d47.gif[/img]

[u][h3]Lily - The Butterfly Spirit[/h3][/u]
Meet [b]Lily[/b], [b]Stella[/b]'s younger sister.

She's here to be your [i]guiding light[/i] by granting you the ability to [b]navigate at night[/b], and by offering a sweet and personal window into several scenes of [b]Stella[/b]'s life. 👀

Note that she'll only appear near the [b]very end of the game[/b], so it might a while before you'll get to actually meet her personally!

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9TGG72zmsA][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/7390db7ea294569cc02752dec74d9089ba90b707.png[/img][/url]
[u][h3]Patch Notes:[/h3][/u]
New Content:
[list][*]Lily can join your boat!
[*]Fishing can now be done in coop! 🎣
[*]Added a new atmosphere to Buck's event.
[*]New coop controller assignment screen.[/list]Quality of Life Update:
[list][*]The boat can now travel at night after the first conversation with [b]Lily[/b]. 
[*]New visual effects when [b]Stanley[/b] is found.
[*]UI now shows how many items can be added to stations.
[*]Recipe collection now shares the same sorting as the recipe book.
[*]Island's names now appear while fast travelling.
[*]Bus Stops are easier to see from the Fast Travel screen.[/list]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/972660/discussions/0/5916017125833664433/]Click here for a list of all the bug fixes![/url]

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/972660/discussions/0/5916017125833664433/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/afcbd33230d88a83cadebf2f1f882e86317ccd5a.gif[/img][/url]
[h2]On to the News![/h2]

[u][h3]500k copies sold![/h3][/u]
[b]Spiritfarer[/b] is officially [b]Thunder Lotus[/b]’ [i]most successful[/i] project to date! Since its launch in [u]August 2020[/u], it sold over 500,000 units worldwide across all systems! ːcat_starsː

But that's not all, [b]Spiritfarer[/b] is still sitting at [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/972660/Spiritfarer/?utm_source=SteamForums&utm_medium=News&utm_campaign=Lily%20Update&utm_content=Lily%20Update][b]Overwhelmingly Positive[/b][/url] reviews thanks to you all! It received nominations at The Game Awards, The DICE Awards, and BAFTA Game Awards, and we [b]won three categories[/b] at the [b]Canadian Game Awards[/b]!

We're eternally thankful for all the support you've given us! Thank you so very much! ːstella_heartsː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35210778/03e58da461cee53bfefd6f5b53f6eeedf81831d8.png[/img]

[u][h3]Gustav update[/h3][/u]
We haven't forgotten about our announcement regarding [url=https://thunderlotusgames.com/an-apology/][b]Gustav[/b]'s story[/url]. We're happy to say that we've collected invaluable feedback from a panel of gamers with disabilities, and will adjust the content accordingly, which we'll implement along with the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/972660/announcements/detail/3040462341844559101?utm_source=SteamForums&utm_medium=News&utm_campaign=Lily%20Update&utm_content=Gustav][b]Beverly[/b] Update[/url] this [b]Summer[/b]. [u][h3]LudoNarraCon[/h3][/u]

notes.title: Music Week: What Debussy can tell us about mood in games
notes.content:
Next on Music Week, a look at how a specific movement in art and music might be an especially good fit for games.

Despite being considered the most important composer in the impressionist movement, Claude Debussy was not fond of the label. "I am trying to do something different, an effect of reality... what the imbeciles call impressionism," Debussy wrote in 1908."A term which is as poorly used as possible, particularly by the critics, since they do not hesitate to apply it to [J.M.W.] Turner, the finest creator of mysterious effects in all the world of art."

Debussy was probably wary of the term due to its dubious art world origins: coined by critic Louis Leroy, it was initially used in a derogatory manner to review an exhibition by painters including Claude Monet and Pierre-Auguste Renoir. "Impressionism" was used to ridicule the painters' loose brush-strokes and casual composition, which Leroy (and many others at the time) considered unfinished. The term was then applied to Debussy's music, with critics finding similarities between the painters' use of contrasting colours, light and blurred backgrounds, and Debussy's use of orchestral colour and harmony to make listeners focus on an overall "impression".

notes.title: 2020's best games gave me the quiet magic I was seeking
notes.content:
Editor's note: Take a breath. We're almost there. 2020's been quite the year, and it's very nearly over. Across the festive break, members of the Eurogamer team and our contributors will be running down their personal top five games of 2020, before we announce our game of the year - and before, of course, we hand over to you for the annual Reader's Top 50. Thanks for being with us this year, and see you on the other side.

In this unnaturally long year, I found myself seeking out games whose worlds were filled with quiet, relaxing, magic. It's the kind of magic that, rather than bombarding you with rules and consequences, slowly envelopes you until the barrier between it and what might be considered normal has dissolved entirely. These games helped me forget what was happening around the world for a while, transporting me instead to places where the wonderfully bizarre is commonplace.

In Spiritfarer I found the magic of discovery; nearly every island has something you need hidden away somewhere on its shores and I started keeping notes on which lands I hadn't been able to fully explore, so that I wouldn't forget to revisit them. Even the sea has its own secrets - I love sailing through the patches of endless night, because the music and change in atmosphere create the idea that, for a short while, you're gazing upon the true nature of this world. My favourite part of Spiritfarer, however, was, in a year where I've spent six months in the same room, it made me feel helpful. You're not just ferrying the dead, you're healing their wounds, soothing their demons and finding the perfect way to help their souls finally rest.

notes.title: Spiritfarer review - a beautiful, unique blend of genres
notes.content:
The ferryman has come to collect Stella for her last journey, on a plane between the land of the living and the afterlife. As she sits in Charon's boat, he gives her one final job - to help a few souls let go of the regrets that anchor them to life and allow them to pass on.

It sounds like a stately job. A cosy, tranquil journey. In reality however, Spiritfarer isn't a journey across calm seas so much as a sprint. You're given your own boat and set off to explore the spirit realm. In its towns and mountain villages you find spirits willing to join you, but before they can actually move on to the afterlife, you need to both build them a space on your boat to enjoy and coax out their story so they may eventually find closure.

Soon, an eclectic group of passengers settles in. Your first passenger, Dawn, for example, is a fawn with fur so plush it looks like she's wearing a stola. She also has a penchant for smoking. Your uncle Atul, a rotund frog, used to be a handyman and loves sharing food with others. Making them feel at home begins with gathering the resources needed to build a personalised cabin for each passenger. Distinct from the in- and outside, these cabins ooze flair and showcase their owners' personalities, but the best thing about them is how they sit on a boat. You stack them on top of each other like a game of management Tetris, and as your boat grows and you gain new buildings, you may have to move them around in order to find a good spot for each. Just watching the stack grow is an amazingly satisfying visual representation of progress. Stella navigates between these buildings like a character in a side-scrolling platformer, and she has similar abilities, too, which isn't surprising given Thunder Lotus' metroidvania roots.

notes.title: Spiritfarer review
notes.content:
Spiritfarer review
Spiritfarer’s cosy management is a thousand acts of kindness, beautifully done. It will make you sad, but it even does that in a kind way.

  • Developer: Thunder Lotus Games
  • Publisher: Thunder Lotus Games
  • Release: August 18th
  • On: Windows, Mac OS X, Linux
  • From: Steam
  • Price: £23.80/€25/$30

Spiritfarer

is about death. You play as Stella, whose job is to take dying spirits through the Everdoor to their final death, when they’re ready. Except, I think it is actually about kindness. Helping a spirit become ready to go involves cooking for them, hugging them, and building them a home on your enormous houseboat. And for that you must care for sheep, play music to plants to help them grow, mine for coal and learn to smelt silver.

It is a cosy management game where you spend most of your time harvesting things to make other things. Like Stardew Valley, but where your thousand acts of labour are done entirely for, on the face of it, nothing. Or at least not for your own material gain. It’s all given away. It is excellent.

notes.title: Spiritfarer is a beautiful game about moving on
notes.content:
In fantasy terms, Spiritfarer has focused on the equivalent of the Grey Havens, the place in The Lord of the Rings where you go and never return. This is a "cozy management game about dying", which is a very appealing pitch. There's a short demo on Steam that you can play right now. Do play it. Spiritfarer is already wonderful.

You play a ferryperson for the deceased. You have a beautiful boat that appears to have all sorts of dwellings built on it. It reminds me a little of the old London Bridge that was teetering with overhanging buildings like Nonesuch House and whatnot. You take people aboard when they are almost ready to move on. You build them rooms to stay in and you do things for them - in the demo you are tasked with going to retrieve a beloved necklace for someone. There is a lot of gadding back and forth across the sea managing things. Plant crops in a little garden. Catch fish and cook for people. Attend to people's moods.

Spiritfarer is trying to do something very difficult, I think. From the demo you spend a lot of time nudging people's moods to where you want them to be. I worried at first that it was a little transactional. But then I started to wonder if, over the full length of the game, the individual bumps and nudges will smooth out. I suspect the people you're ferrying are not the true passengers, in other words. I suspect that Spiritfarer is trying to make something happen on your side of the screen, as you witness these people moving on and engage with what you are a part of.

notes.title: On love, death, sustaining an indie studio and following Keanu Reeves onstage
notes.content:
"It's something epic, but something beautiful," says William Dub when asked to explain the etymology of his studio's name, Thunder Lotus. "To me that combination of a thunderstorm that's big powerful and scary, and then the lotus flower which is something very delicate, and really beautiful. And it sounds really cool too! One of [our aims] is to make beautifully powerful games. I think that really reflects the name of the studio."

Thunder Lotus might not be a name you're super familiar with just yet, but they're an emerging talent - first with 2015's Jotun, then with the lavish Metroidvania Sundered and now with Spiritfarer, an ambitious, curious little adventure that caused ripples when it broke cover at Microsoft's E3 conference back in June.

"It's something we'd been driving towards since the beginning of the studio, and to have that opportunity was really special. We were onstage after Keanu Reeves! It was Cyberpunk, Keanu Reeves and then Spiritfarer - and now I've got an awesome story for my friends, if they don't understand gaming. It's the Super Bowl of gaming! We're onstage after Keanu Reeves! They're like oh my god, then they understand the reach and magnitude of it all."

notes.title: Spiritfarer's response to grief is a warm embrace
notes.content:
Last month, one of my close family members passed away. It wasn't a surprise: he'd reached 90, his health was deteriorating, and we all knew it wouldn't be long until it happened. But no matter how prepared you are, it's always a shock - and on the evening I found out, I spent several hours on the shorefront trying to process my grief.

When we describe death, it's nearly always in negative terms, and loaded with imagery of things like tombstones, skulls and the colour black. Death is the Other we define ourselves against, and even the language we use to describe death ('passed away') distances us from the concept.

Most of the time, we just don't talk about it.

notes.title: Introducing Spiritfarer
notes.content:
[h1]A cozy management game about dying[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32943393/6376b80db970593c6781aae309e2c50d6f011741.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone!

It’s a big red letter day here at Thunder Lotus! We’re super stoked to finally reveal the project we’ve been lovingly crafting over the past 18 months or so. Behold [i]Spiritfarer[/i]: a cozy management game about dying.

Queue our first trailer and prepare thyselves for the feels!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YnuEvePlxWI

[i]Spiritfarer [/i]is a project that’s near and dear to our hearts. Here’s the basic pitch:

In [i]Spiritfarer[/i], you play Stella, ferrymaster to the deceased. Build a boat to explore the world, then befriend and care for spirits before finally releasing them into the afterlife. Farm, mine, fish, harvest, cook, and craft your way across mystical seas. Join the adventure as Daffodil the cat, in two-player cooperative play. Spend relaxing quality time with your spirit passengers, create lasting memories, and, ultimately, learn how to say goodbye to your cherished friends.

Expect a release next year on Steam, as well as with Xbox Game Pass for PC and Console, Xbox One, PS4, and Nintendo Switch!

We can’t wait to tell you more about the game over the next few days, weeks, and months.

Today, as I write this, we’re enjoying the frenzy of [b]E3 2019[/b], where we’ve been invited by the good people at Microsoft to present the first playable demo of [i]Spiritfarer [/i]as part of their E3 activities. Come say hi at the Microsoft Theater if you’re in town for the convention! If not, maybe we’re coming to another con near you over the next few months, hmm? 

Stay tuned (and do please [b]Follow [/b]or Wishlist [i]Spiritfarer[/i])!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/972660/Spiritfarer/

Back to you soon with more Spiritfarer news!

Cheers y’all,

– Rodrigue and the Thunder Lotus team
